item.title: fountain transformation
item.description:
I'm feeling that I reached my limit with ballpoint pens, or at least for now. I am fully submerged in black permanent ink. Three fountain pens by nib size and a Kuretake brush pen all feeding from the one ink pot. The limit, by the way, I meet regularly. Sometimes because I lack the instructions, yet sometimes it is precisely the instructions that show me the door.

A few years ago I became fascinated with cornets. It was before Christmas in Durham, staying with my inlaws. The freezing December wind from the North Sea, the jazz records my father in law played, the smell of coal burning, the street brass bands, I was swimming in horns. In a second hand shop I spotted an old beaten up cornet, so I decided to buy it and have a go. On the bus on the way home, the crowd possesed by the Christmas spook were encouraging our children as they tried to blow a sound out of the old metal tube to no avail. The instrument was finally passed to Martha, then three, and she blew a perfect rumbling C and the crowd cheered.

item.title: Still going
item.description: Recently I retold a story that I forgot about for a long time. I must have told it many times around the time it actually happened. This time I've noticed some gaps that I did not know how to fill, and I was getting this odd feeling: "perhaps this never happened?". I was puzzled as I don't make up such stories; I have no reason to, I find enough interest and weirdness in reality not to come up with lies. Well, judge for yourself:

item.title: Ink characters
item.description:
I really don't know where those characters appeared from. When they first crossed my pen, each and every one, I found them embarrassing. They suggest what I did not want to suggest, what I never meant to say. And it is not that by that they uncovered some truth I was trying to conceal, they surprised me with their naive inadequacy. Going through them again after more than a year, they also seem incomplete, the artist impatient, the technique half arsed.
Well, enough with that, they are what they are.

item.title: Mountain Ink
item.description: I used to mostly draw from references, but this year I've started drawing from imagination. I discovered that there is so much recorded in my head, I had no idea. It is a work in progress, I can't say that I am completely happy with the drawings, besides proportions and perspective and shading, I don't understand where those images come from. Some of them are right down embarrasing, all of them are strange, but more about that in a different post. in this post I would like to say goodbye to some drawings made with references, either photograps I took, or photographs in books.
